column6: Worked: X1,X2,X3 give syndromes 10,11,01; Z1 commutes with both. OLD TEXT (not fixed): Explainer says Steane uses C1 = C2 = Hamming [7,4,3]; wrong, C2 = C1^perp ([7,3,4]); with C1 = C2 the code would encode k = 0.
Worked all four: I,X,Z,XZ give Phi+,Psi+,Phi-,-Psi-; CNOT then H gives 00,01,10,-11.

Exercise failed when worked: "extend into a chain" unspecified; a chain along adjacent lattice edges shades every plaquette beside it, not just the ends. "Joins opposite boundaries" works only for the boundary pair whose edges touch one plaquette. Fixed: each new edge shares the last plaquette reached; ends on edges that belong to only one plaquette. OLD TEXT: Q2 explanation says logical failure scales as p^d; it is ~p^(d/2) (decoder fails past ~d/2 errors), as the file's own (p/p_th)^(d/2) says. Explainer says logical X joins rough boundaries; with its plaquette = Z convention, X strings end without syndrome at smooth boundaries (Dennis et al.); check convention.

Worked: B12 ~ exp(-i pi/4 Z) (S up to phase), B23 ~ exp(-i pi/4 X); S and Rx(pi/2) do not commute. OLD TEXT: Explainer "zero effect" on computation overstates (it later says exponentially suppressed); Q3 explanation "abelian anyons cannot encode quantum information" overstates (toric-code ground space on a torus does); banned words "crucial"/"Crucially" in old Q3 explanation and Explainer.
Worked: <Z>=cos t, <X>=sin t; E = sqrt2 sin(t+pi/4), min -sqrt2 at 5pi/4; eigenvalues of X+Z are +-sqrt2.
